{{Short description|Theory in physics}}
{{string theory}}

In mathematics, specifically [[algebraic geometry]], '''Donaldson–Thomas theory''' is the theory of '''Donaldson–Thomas invariants'''.   Given a [[compact space|compact]] [[moduli space]] of [[sheaf (mathematics)|sheaves]] on a [[Calabi–Yau manifold|Calabi–Yau]] threefold, its Donaldson–Thomas invariant is the virtual number of its points, i.e., the integral of the cohomology class 1 against the [[virtual fundamental class]].  The Donaldson–Thomas invariant is a [[Holomorphic function|holomorphic]] analogue of the [[Casson invariant]].  The invariants were introduced by {{harvs|txt|authorlink= Simon Donaldson|first=Simon|last=Donaldson|author2-link= Richard Thomas (mathematician)|first2=Richard|last2= Thomas|year=1998}}. Donaldson–Thomas invariants have close connections to [[Gromov–Witten invariant]]s of algebraic three-folds and the theory of stable pairs due to [[Rahul Pandharipande]] and Thomas. 

Donaldson–Thomas theory is physically motivated by certain [[Bogomol'nyi–Prasad–Sommerfield state|BPS states]] that occur in [[string theory|string]] and [[gauge theory]]<ref>{{Cite arXiv|last=Bridgeland |first=Tom |date=2006-02-08 |title=Stability conditions on triangulated categories |eprint=math/0212237}}</ref><sup>pg 5</sup>. This is due to the fact the invariants depend on a [[Bridgeland stability condition|stability condition]] on the derived category <math>D^b(\mathcal{M})</math> of the moduli spaces being studied. Essentially, these stability conditions correspond to points in the Kähler moduli space of a Calabi-Yau manifold, as considered in [[Mirror symmetry conjecture|mirror symmetry]], and the resulting subcategory <math>\mathcal{P} \subset D^b(\mathcal{M})</math> is the category of BPS states for the corresponding [[Super conformal field theory|SCFT]].

==Definition and examples==
The basic idea of [[Gromov–Witten invariant]]s is to probe the geometry of a space by studying pseudoholomorphic maps from [[Riemann surface]]s to a smooth target. The moduli stack of all such maps admits a virtual fundamental class, and intersection theory on this stack yields numerical invariants that can often contain enumerative information. In similar spirit, the approach of Donaldson–Thomas theory is to study curves in an algebraic three-fold by their equations. More accurately, by studying ideal sheaves on a space. This moduli space also admits a virtual fundamental class and yields certain numerical invariants that are enumerative.

Whereas in Gromov–Witten theory, maps are allowed to be multiple covers and collapsed components of the domain curve, Donaldson–Thomas theory allows for nilpotent information contained in the sheaves, however, these are integer valued invariants. There are deep conjectures due to [[Davesh Maulik]], [[Andrei Okounkov]], [[Nikita Nekrasov]] and [[Rahul Pandharipande]], proved in increasing generality, that Gromov–Witten and Donaldson–Thomas theories of algebraic three-folds are actually equivalent.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=D. |last1=Maulik |first2=N. |last2=Nekrasov |first3=A. |last3=Okounkov |first4=R. |last4=Pandharipande |title=Gromov–Witten theory and Donaldson–Thomas theory, I |journal=Compositio Mathematica |volume=142 |issue=5 |year=2006 |pages=1263–1285 |doi=10.1112/S0010437X06002302 |arxiv=math/0312059 |s2cid=5760317 }}</ref> More concretely, their generating functions are equal after an appropriate change of variables. For Calabi–Yau threefolds, the Donaldson–Thomas invariants can be formulated as weighted Euler characteristic on the moduli space. There have also been recent connections between these invariants, the motivic Hall algebra, and the ring of functions on the quantum torus.<ref>{{cite book | last=Bridgeland | first=Tom |editor-last=De Fernex | editor-first=Tommaso |  title=Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics | chapter=Hall algebras and Donaldson-Thomas invariants | publisher=American Mathematical Society | publication-place=Providence, Rhode Island | volume=97.1 | date=1 June 2018 | isbn=978-1-4704-3577-6 | doi=10.1090/pspum/097.1/01670 | doi-access=free | pages=75–100}}</ref>

*The moduli space of lines on the [[quintic threefold]] is a discrete set of 2875 points.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Harris | first=Joe |author-link=Joe Harris (mathematician) | title=Galois groups of enumerative problems | journal=Duke Mathematical Journal | volume=46 | issue=4 | date=1 December 1979 | issn=0012-7094 | doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-79-04635-0 | pages=685–724}}</ref>  The virtual number of points is the actual number of points, and hence the Donaldson–Thomas invariant of this moduli space is the integer 2875.
*Similarly, the Donaldson–Thomas invariant of the moduli space of [[conic]]s on the quintic is 609250.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Katz | first=Sheldon |author-link=Sheldon Katz | title=On the finiteness of rational curves on quintic threefolds | journal=Compositio Mathematica | publisher=Martinus Nijhoff Publishers | volume=60 | issue=2 | date=11 August 2010 | issn=0010-437X | pages=151–162 | url=https://eudml.org/doc/89802 | access-date=20 November 2024}}</ref>

=== Definition ===
For a Calabi–Yau threefold <math>Y</math><ref>{{cite book  | last = Szendrői | first = Balázs|editor-last1=Bouchard | editor-first1=Vincent |editor-last2=Doran | editor-first2=Charles  |editor-last3=Méndez-Diez | editor-first3=Stefan |editor-last4=Quigley | editor-first4=Callum|chapter=Cohomological Donaldson–Thomas theory | title=String-Math 2014 - Conference Proceedings | series = Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics| publisher=American Mathematical Society | publication-place=Providence, Rhode Island | volume=93 | date=9 June 2016 | isbn=978-1-4704-1992-9  | mr = 3526001 | pages = 363–396 | arxiv = 1503.07349 | doi=10.1090/pspum/093 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Thomas | first = R. P.
 | arxiv = math/9806111
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Journal of Differential Geometry
 | mr = 1818182
 | pages = 367–438
 | title = A holomorphic Casson invariant for Calabi-Yau 3-folds, and bundles on $K3$ fibrations
 | url = https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.jdg/1214341649
 | volume = 54
 | year = 2000| doi = 10.4310/jdg/1214341649
 }}</ref> and a fixed cohomology class <math>\alpha \in H^{\text{even}}(Y,\mathbb{Q})</math> there is an associated moduli stack <math>\mathcal{M}(Y,\alpha)</math> of coherent sheaves with Chern character <math>c(\mathcal{E}) = \alpha</math>. In general, this is a non-separated Artin stack of infinite type which is difficult to define numerical invariants upon it. Instead, there are open substacks <math>\mathcal{M}^{\sigma}(Y,\alpha)</math> parametrizing such coherent sheaves <math>\mathcal{E}</math> which have a stability condition <math>\sigma</math> imposed upon them, i.e. <math>\sigma</math>-stable sheaves. These moduli stacks have much nicer properties, such as being separated of finite type. The only technical difficulty is they can have bad singularities due to the existence of obstructions of deformations of a fixed sheaf. In particular<blockquote><math>\begin{align}
T_{[\mathcal{E}]}\mathcal{M}^\sigma(Y,\alpha) &\cong \text{Ext}^1(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{E}) \\
\text{Ob}_{[\mathcal{E}]}(\mathcal{M}^\sigma(Y,\alpha)) &\cong \text{Ext}^2(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{E})

\end{align}</math></blockquote>Now because <math>Y</math> is Calabi–Yau, Serre duality implies<blockquote><math>\text{Ext}^2(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{E}) \cong \text{Ext}^1(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{E}\otimes\omega_Y)^\vee \cong \text{Ext}^1(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{E})^\vee</math></blockquote>which gives a perfect obstruction theory of dimension 0. In particular, this implies the associated virtual fundamental class<blockquote><math>[\mathcal{M}^\sigma(Y,\alpha)]^{vir} \in H_0(\mathcal{M}^\sigma(Y,\alpha), \mathbb{Z})</math></blockquote>is in homological degree <math>0</math>. We can then define the '''DT invariant''' as<blockquote><math>\int_{[\mathcal{M}^\sigma(Y,\alpha)]^{vir}}1</math></blockquote>which depends upon the stability condition <math>\sigma</math> and the cohomology class <math>\alpha</math>. It was proved by Thomas that for a smooth family <math>Y_t</math> the invariant defined above does not change. At the outset researchers chose the Gieseker stability condition, but other DT-invariants in recent years have been studied based on other stability conditions, leading to wall-crossing formulas.<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Kontsevich |first1=Maxim |last2=Soibelman |first2=Yan |date=2008-11-16 |title=Stability structures, motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants and cluster transformations |class=math.AG |eprint=0811.2435}}</ref>

== Facts ==
*The Donaldson–Thomas invariant of the moduli space ''M'' is equal to the weighted [[Euler characteristic]] of ''M''.  The weight function associates to every point in ''M'' an analogue of the [[Milnor number]] of a hyperplane singularity.

== Generalizations ==
* Instead of moduli spaces of sheaves, one considers moduli spaces of [[derived category]] objects. That gives the [[Pandharipande–Thomas invariant]]s that count stable pairs of a Calabi–Yau 3-fold.
* Instead of integer valued invariants, one considers [[motive (algebraic geometry)|motivic]] invariants.
